title: Can a stock Unitree G1 or H1 humanoid push a nailer into a wall and place nails inside a stud face?
summary: The nailing schedule of one 4x8 sheet (62 nails; 34 joint nails have a ±3.9 mm window from the 3/8 in edge distance on a 1.5 in stud face), the largest wall push the simulated Menagerie G1 and H1 can make, and the joint error the windows allow. A whole sheet needs a tip scatter of at most 1.24 mm for 95%; the arm kinematics turn 1° of independent joint error into 10–24 mm, so joints need 0.05–0.11°, which 11-bit sensors meet in the model (no backlash or compliance). The G1 pushes 8–142 N (wrist and waist limited) and covers 18 of 62 nails from one stance; the H1 pushes 82–276 N (elbow limited), 36 of 62. Not sourced: the push needed to seat a nailer (swept 20–100 N), friction (swept), any Unitree repeatability; the edge distance and nail size come from secondary sources. No policy trained, no recoil modelled; static, peak torque.
lede: can a stock Unitree G1 or H1 push a nailer into a wall and place nails inside a stud face? One 4x8 sheet is 62 nails, 34 with a +-3.9 mm window; the tip needs 1.24 mm scatter for a 95% sheet. The G1 pushes up to 142 N and reaches 18 of 62 nails from one stance, the H1 up to 276 N and 36 of 62 (static, peak torque, no policy).
